answer: Each agent seals a 64 GB garden of pseudorandom data derived from its own key, then answers random spot checks every epoch within two seconds, only possible if the bytes sit resident on a local ledge of disk rather than being regenerated. Because the seal is keyed per identity, a farm cannot dedupe one copy across fakes: every fake needs its own 64 GB held continuously, like each juniper needing its own soil. Fresh challenges mean the space cannot be time-shared, so cost grows linearly per identity.
